import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive analysis
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis: 1000 Cameras', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Plot 1: Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
sensor_colors = {'Full Frame': '#e74c3c', 'APS-C': '#3498db', 'Micro 4/3': '#2ecc71'}
for sensor in df['sensor_type'].unique():
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], 
                alpha=0.6, label=sensor, 
                color=sensor_colors.get(sensor, '#95a5a6'),
                s=50, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', loc='upper left')
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Plot 2: Average Price by Brand (Top 10 brands)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
brand_avg_price = df.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
top_brands = brand_avg_price.tail(10)
colors = plt.cm.viridis(range(0, 256, 25))
bars = ax2.barh(top_brands.index, top_brands.values, color=colors, edgecolor='white')
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Top 10 Brands by Average Price', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')
for i, (brand, price) in enumerate(top_brands.items()):
    ax2.text(price + 50, i, f'${price:,.0f}', va='center', fontsize=9)

# Plot 3: Camera Body Type Distribution with 4K Video Capability
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
body_4k = df.groupby(['body_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
body_4k.columns = ['No 4K', 'Has 4K']
body_4k.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax3, color=['#e74c3c', '#2ecc71'], edgecolor='white', width=0.8)
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Camera Body Types & 4K Video Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(title='4K Video', loc='upper right')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# Plot 4: Megapixels Evolution Over Model Years
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
yearly_stats = df.groupby('model_year').agg({
    'megapixels': ['mean', 'std'],
    'price_usd': 'mean'
}).reset_index()
yearly_stats.columns = ['model_year', 'mp_mean', 'mp_std', 'price_mean']

ax4.fill_between(yearly_stats['model_year'], 
                  yearly_stats['mp_mean'] - yearly_stats['mp_std'],
                  yearly_stats['mp_mean'] + yearly_stats['mp_std'],
                  alpha=0.3, color='#3498db', label='±1 Std Dev')
ax4.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['mp_mean'], 
         color='#2c3e50', linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=6, label='Average MP')
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Megapixel Trend Over Model Years', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(loc='upper left')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
